policy: Use references to extract principles and compare interaction patterns. Do not copy source code, assets, copywriting or complete compositions.

references.name: Impeccable
references.adaptation: Use specialized design intents and deterministic review; keep Integra contracts and evidence explicit.
references.licenseNote: Review upstream license and notices before reusing code. This catalog links and documents concepts only.
useWhen: A structured design-review workflow, iterative critique or a precise anti-pattern vocabulary is needed.
notFor: Selecting a product's brand, palette or typography without project context.
Treating upstream commands as normative UI requirements.

references.name: REA — Reverse Engineer Anything
references.adaptation: Apply the method to permitted UI behavior and references; binary analysis is out of scope.
references.licenseNote: Link to upstream documentation; do not copy unrelated implementation.
useWhen: An evidence-led investigation plan, traceability or a clear adapter boundary is needed.
notFor: Treating REA as a visual design system.
Using techniques beyond permitted access or task scope.

references.name: Agent Skills specification
useWhen: Designing portable skill metadata, progressive disclosure or host-agnostic skill packaging.
notFor: Claiming a host loaded a skill without testing that host.
Deciding product UI styling.

references.name: WCAG 2.2
references.adaptation: Use normative criteria and exceptions; do not claim full-page conformance from partial checks.
useWhen: Assessing a named WCAG 2.2 success criterion or accessibility requirement.
notFor: Choosing a visual theme or claiming full conformance from a partial check.
Replacing platform-specific assistive-technology testing.

references.name: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide
references.adaptation: Prefer native HTML first; use ARIA patterns only when custom widgets are necessary.
useWhen: Implementing custom composite widgets, roles, keyboard patterns or state behavior.
notFor: Adding ARIA where native HTML provides the needed semantics.
Treating a pattern example as a finished production component.

references.name: Material Design 3
references.adaptation: Study token and state modeling; do not apply its visual language to every product.
useWhen: Studying semantic tokens, component states, adaptive layout or motion systems.
notFor: Applying Material's brand language to unrelated products by default.
Assuming its components match another stack or platform.

references.name: Apple Human Interface Guidelines
references.adaptation: Use when the target is an Apple-platform experience.
useWhen: The target is an Apple platform or must follow its navigation, input and interaction conventions.
notFor: Treating Apple-specific patterns as universal web requirements.
Using it as the only authority for a non-Apple platform.

references.name: Shopify Polaris
references.adaptation: Study task-oriented admin patterns and feedback without replicating branding.
useWhen: Designing merchant/admin workflows, product management, orders or commerce operations.
notFor: Copying Shopify's visual identity or assuming every storefront has merchant-admin needs.
Replacing verified local checkout or payment requirements.

references.name: Microsoft Fluent 2
references.adaptation: Reference for enterprise interaction states and system consistency.
useWhen: Evaluating enterprise density, cross-platform component states or accessible system consistency.
notFor: Applying Fluent styling as the default for unrelated products.
Assuming one density suits every role.

references.name: GOV.UK Design System
references.adaptation: Prioritize clarity and task completion for high-consequence service flows.
useWhen: Designing public-service forms, eligibility, plain language, error recovery or consequential journeys.
notFor: Treating UK policy content as valid in another jurisdiction.
Copying government branding or claiming legal compliance.

references.name: Radix Primitives
references.adaptation: Use primitives where the target stack calls for them; inspect behavior, not just appearance.
useWhen: A React project uses Radix and needs dialogs, menus, popovers or keyboard primitives.
notFor: Adding Radix without an architectural reason.
Assuming styling is included or that a primitive replaces product testing.

references.name: shadcn/ui
references.adaptation: Treat components as source-owned building blocks; customize rather than accepting defaults wholesale.
useWhen: The project uses shadcn/ui or needs source-owned composable React components and token integration.
notFor: Assuming shadcn/ui is installed in every project.
Using defaults wholesale without adapting them.

references.name: Tailwind CSS
references.adaptation: Respect the target project's actual Tailwind version and config.
useWhen: The inspected project uses Tailwind and its actual version/configuration is known.
notFor: Writing utility classes for a different styling system.
Assuming examples from another major version are compatible.

references.name: MDN Accessibility
references.adaptation: Use primary browser documentation for semantics and APIs.
useWhen: Checking semantic HTML, accessible names, browser behavior or a web API implementation detail.
notFor: Using MDN instead of normative accessibility criteria or assistive-technology testing.
Inferring behavior in a browser/version that was not tested.

references.name: Web Vitals
references.adaptation: Use measured metrics from representative sessions.
useWhen: Interpreting Core Web Vitals definitions or a measured performance report.
notFor: Making performance claims without representative measurements.
Treating generic thresholds as proof of a particular site's performance.

usagePolicy.selectByQuestion: Choose a source only when it can answer the exact design, interaction, implementation or quality question being decided.
usagePolicy.sourcePrecedence: Use normative standards for requirements; official technical/platform documentation for behavior; official design systems for their documented patterns; product examples for directly observed behavior; methodology repositories for process inspiration.
usagePolicy.quantity: Normally use one to three relevant references. Do not add sources merely to decorate a brief.
usagePolicy.verification: Every entry is a catalog-only lead until its specific page or section has been inspected. Keep lastVerifiedAt null until live verification is recorded.
usagePolicy.evidence: Record exact page/section, date, observed behavior, evidence class, confidence and limitation. A URL or title alone is not evidence.
usagePolicy.adaptation: Extract and adapt a principle to the target product. Never copy source code, assets, copywriting, proprietary components or complete compositions.
